correctness.rationale: The four-overlap-state de Bruijn graph has exactly one path for each finite input predecessor. Initial path counts (1,1,1,1) and exact min(2, linear-transfer) updates retain the invariant that every coordinate equals the true terminal path count capped at two. Hence total 1 is equivalent to a single complete finite predecessor. Every state belongs to {0,1,2}^4; exhaustive BFS closure at all 256 rules (maximum reached 66) proves the classifications for arbitrary output length, and no unseen longer singleton can exist for the 92 absent cases. Exhaustive independent direct input enumeration for all 32,256 length<=6 rule/output pairs verifies predicted unique words, witnesses and terminal pair supports, and rerunning the saved verifier byte-compares all 256 catalog rows. Histogram: 16,52,56,28,4,8,92. Eight sharp rules 37,57,91,99,156,164,198,218. Full unique predecessors imply right-boundary uniqueness, giving exactly 42 right-only rules and shortest-length gaps 132,20,8,4. No assertion about periodic or global bilateral inverse uniqueness.

value.rationale: Finite observation that determines all hidden input bits is an intrinsically motivated observability invariant of one-step cellular automata. The all-256 spectrum is a natural complete classification, identifies eight sharp extremizers at six symbols, and exactly separates the 42 rules where a one-sided boundary is recoverable but an entire finite preimage never is; this separation shows a genuine hierarchy of inverse information instead of an arbitrary finite slice. The finite closure proves impossibility at ALL lengths and provides a compact independently reproducible algorithm, not a mere enumeration of sample length six. No implication beyond binary radius-one one-step finite-open-boundary preimages is claimed.
